title: Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Service Standard — Uplift for Late-Posted Card-Paid Segments
content:
**Standard.** When the points of a flown card-paid segment of a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement are posted, the posting delay adds to the card-paid uplift. The posting delay is the number of calendar days from the date the card-paid ticket was flown — the date its record in Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand shows the ticket reaching flown — to the posting date.

| Posting delay | Addition to the card-paid uplift |
|---|---|
| 30 calendar days or more | 20 percentage points |
| 14 calendar days or more, and fewer than 30 | 10 percentage points |
| fewer than 14 calendar days | nothing |

**How the card-paid uplift acts.** The card-paid uplift is counted in percentage points; uplifts on different grounds are added together, and the segment's earned card-paid segment points are raised by the total: the points posted are the earned points multiplied by one hundred plus the card-paid uplift, divided by one hundred, rounded down to the whole point once at the end.

### Boundary days (hypothetical dates)

| Ticket flown on | Posted on | Delay | Addition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 31 March | 30 days | 20 points |
| 1 March | 30 March | 29 days | 10 points |
| 1 March | 15 March | 14 days | 10 points |
| 1 March | 14 March | 13 days | nothing |

A segment with earned points of 636 and a delay of 35 days, with no other uplift, posts 636 multiplied by 120 and divided by one hundred, which is 763.2, rounded down to 763 points.
